name: Mauritius
title: Holidays in Mauritius
intro: Lagoon beaches, giant tortoises and rainbow-coloured sand in the Indian Ocean. Here's what Mauritius is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.

facts.label: Time difference
facts.value: 3 to 4 hrs ahead of the UK

facts_note: Mauritius drives on the left, like the UK. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: April to May and September to December are ideal, warm and fairly dry. June to August is the cooler winter, still in the mid-20s but breezier. January to March is hot and humid, with a chance of cyclones.

things.name: Casela Nature Park
things.blurb: Walk with giant tortoises and see big cats, with zip lines for older children.

things.name: Chamarel
things.blurb: Seven Coloured Earth dunes and a tall waterfall in the south-west.

things.name: Black River Gorges
things.blurb: Rainforest walks with viewpoints and rare birds.

things.name: Île aux Cerfs
things.blurb: A boat to an island with calm, shallow lagoon beaches.

things.name: Glass-bottom boat
things.blurb: See the reef and fish without getting wet. Good for little ones.

things.name: Le Morne
things.blurb: A beautiful lagoon beach under a dramatic mountain.

faqs.question: Is Mauritius good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. Lagoons protected by reefs make the sea calm and shallow, and many resorts have great kids clubs. English is widely spoken.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Ten to fourteen nights, as the flight is about twelve hours.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: No, British passport holders can visit for a holiday without a visa. Check GOV.UK for the current rules.

faqs.question: Which coast is best?
faqs.answer: The north and west are sunnier and calmer in winter. The east is breezier but cooler in summer. The south is wilder and less built-up.
